_comment: B1 + B3 of docs/2026-09-07_anytime_prediction_and_calibrated_eta_design.zh.md (§三). BASE = L1_native32's content — custom, N=32, simple-v3's own supervision (native segment endpoints, true-time-position, imitation 64, velocity 0.003), the DETERMINISTIC point-estimate base and deliberately NOT the latent one: TSConfig refuses duration_head=quantile with latent_dim>0 (z reaches the duration by shifting the point head's single logit, and under a posterior sample the quantiles would be conditioned on the flight's own future — an interval B2 could not honestly calibrate). The only change is duration_head=quantile, so the run is `custom` (the recipes pin the head at `point`) and its name carries T=q5. WHAT EACH ARM MEASURES. B1_quantile isolates the head: it emits DURATION_QUANTILES (0.1/0.25/0.5/0.75/0.9), the median walks the existing final_time_s contract (it IS the duration the rollout flies), and the loss swaps the squared final-time residual for the sum of five pinball losses under the SAME component name and the SAME weight. B3_quantile_cta adds cta_conditioning=given so the CTA-conditioned decoder is trained (the rollout flies the truth duration in training, exactly as L3 built it) while the quantile head trains as a TARGET beside it; at predict `--cta-from-quantiles` decodes each flight at its OWN q_tau, so its top-1 reads no future, wears cta=self-q and IS quotable — unlike L3_cta, which is the oracle ceiling this arm is read against. NOT A CLEAN ONE-AXIS ISOLATION, AND THE SIZE OF THE CONFOUND IS STATED: at final_time_scale_s=600 and the same final_time_loss_weight=1.0, the point term and the five pinball terms are not the same size. Computed on B0's measured native32 signed final-time error (p10 -42.3 / p50 +3.5 / p90 +38.3 s, fitted as a normal: mu 3.5 s, sigma 31.4 s), the point term mean((r/scale)^2) is 2.78e-3 while a perfectly calibrated head's sum of five pinball terms is 7.26e-2 — a factor of 26 (about 40 if the point term is read at the MAE rather than the RMS; the same order either way). The pinball gradient is also CONSTANT in the residual where the squared one is proportional to it. So this arm changes the duration term's effective weight and its gradient shape as well as its form, and that is disclosed rather than rescaled: rescaling would make the arm incomparable to every published simple-v* run, which all carry final_time_loss_weight=1.0. CONDITIONAL THIRD ARM, PRE-REGISTERED HERE AND RUN ONLY IF NEEDED: if gate 1 fails, or if pooled ADE moves beyond seed noise, add {"key": "B1_point_matched", "label": "point head at the pinball-matched duration weight", "overrides": {"duration_head": "point", "final_time_loss_weight": 26.0}} to `arms` and re-run — it separates 'the quantile head is worse' from 'the duration term got 26x heavier'. 26.0 is the factor above: a MATCH POINT, not a tuned dose. It is not in `arms` now because running it unconditionally would be a dose sweep nobody asked for. PRE-REGISTERED GATES (§三 3.4). (1) B1: q50's duration error is within seed noise of L1_native32's 25.9 s MAE, and pooled ADE is not worse than native32's 1322 m. (2) B2: the DEPLOYED coverage — the `deployed` block of run_ts_eta_calibration.py's readout, which assigns every held-out flight the delta its own stratum precedence actually gives it, fall-through included — lands in [0.76, 0.84] for the 80 % interval and [0.45, 0.55] for the 50 % one. NOT the per-stratum rows: those measure each delta on its own stratum's members, and a stratum that refused for thinness sends its flights to the pooled delta, about which the pooled row says nothing. Read the fall-through group's own line beside the pooled number. (3) B3: among the flights whose truth duration falls inside [q10, q90], the truth path's chamfer to the NEAREST of the five decoded trajectories is below its chamfer to q50 (run_ts_quantile_fan_readout.py, column 'min<q50'); that readout's 'cal.hit' column is IN-SAMPLE on a val arm and is marked as such — it is not the coverage gate. B3's top-1 is compared to native32 (1322 / vectored 2870) AND to L3_cta's 841 (vectored 1596), which is the perfect-ETA ceiling, not a working point. VETO (same as L2's): straight-in top-1 FDE degraded beyond seed noise on either arm; and B2's own veto — a calibrated median interval width above 120 s in the vectored stratum means T's uncertainty is not something calibration can collect, and the line goes back to A. B0's measured |dt| p80 (vectored 65.8-72.5 s, straight-in 12.0-20.3 s) says a symmetric 80 % interval starts at roughly twice that, so this veto has about a factor of one in hand. WHAT THE COVERAGE NUMBER IS NOT: the calibration split is also the split the checkpoint was selected on (LR schedule, best epoch, early stopping), so this is an empirically measured cross-half coverage and NOT a finite-sample guarantee; the coupling runs through a trajectory metric (common-grid ADE), not the duration residual these deltas are quantiles of. The guarantee-bearing read is pre-registered as a single held-out test-split measurement at the freeze-test ledger stage, not now. THE CALIBRATION STEP IS NOT OPTIONAL AND IS NOT PART OF TRAINING — between train and the final predict, per arm: `python run_ts_eta_calibration.py --checkpoint $C/<ARM>/checkpoint.pt --out $C/<ARM>_calibration` (val only; it writes the conformal table into that checkpoint's own checkpoint_metadata.json, which is what makes predict stamp source.durationIntervalS instead of calibrated:false). Never pass --limit for a table meant to be deployed: it fits the delta on a PREFIX of the split, and the sidecar refuses such a table unless --allow-smoke-table is given deliberately. Predict RE-RUN after calibrating is what produces the calibrated records; a directory predicted before the table exists says calibrated:false and is not wrong, just uncalibrated. The calibrated interval ENDPOINTS are a separate opt-in at predict (--interval-endpoints): the fan gate reads the five quantile leaves, so the endpoints are an extra arm to look at rather than part of it.
